title: The sisters in the bower
summary: Mòrag nic Dhòmhnaill rides to Cathair dhearg and asks her sister to command or forbid the crossing. The queen answers that the crown has never sent anyone anywhere, nor kept back anyone free, and will not begin with her sister.

title: The queen's word sent to the harbours
summary: The queen's word, written by Murchadh mac Eòghainn and sealed, goes by rider to Seann Skell and every harbour of the west and to the vein-house: the crown will send no one and keep no one back, and will judge any quarrel of the venture by the old law.

title: The word read at the harbour-house door
summary: Calum mac Nèill reads the queen's word twice from the harbour-house door to the town standing in the rain. Few cheer; most had wanted the crown to choose for them.

title: The queen's word made a song
summary: On the quay at Seann Skell the fishers say the queen's word over until it becomes a line of song: I will send no one over, and I will keep no one back. The harbour songs keep it so.

title: Aonghas mac Fhionnlaigh says yes
summary: At Inis àrsaidh Mòrag's husband, Aonghas mac Fhionnlaigh, a farmer of the land up the river, agrees that their household will go before she has finished asking.

title: The custodians dispute the right of those who go
summary: Through the winter the custodians at the vein-house argue whether the right to the coal goes with a hearth that crosses the sea or is struck on the day it sails. Fearchar mac Ruairidh holds that the right lives in the hands.

title: The roll copied for the vein-house
summary: The harbour scribe's son copies the roll of the willing onto skin, with a flame-mark beside each household that holds the right to the coal, and sends it up the coal-road to the vein-house.

title: Fearchar mac Ruairidh's household on the roll
summary: Fearchar mac Ruairidh tells the custodians, after the second count, that he entered his own household on the roll at Seann Skell in the moon of Samhnas and ticked his own name twice.
